chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), regarding

two men insulting each other, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The initiator among them is more unjust, and his burden (of sin) and the burden of his companion are upon him, as long as the oppressed one does not transgress.'
ai.seo_question: Who bears more sin when two people insult each other?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him), the initiator of the insult is deemed more unjust, bearing not only their own sin but also that of the responder, provided the latter does not exceed the bounds of reciprocity. This principle underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the 'badī' (initiator) carrying the primary weight of moral fault in mutual disputes, encouraging restraint even when provoked. It serves as a practical guide for maintaining social harmony by discouraging escalation and highlighting the spiritual danger of being the first to transgress.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> regarding

two men insulting (each other). So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The initiator is more unjust from the two, and his burden (of sin) and the burden of his companion would be upon him for as long as the oppressed one does not transgress’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from abu al-Hassan Musa (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Two people were abusing each other and the Imam said, ‘The initiator is more unjust. His own sins and the sins of his companion are on him as long as the oppressed one does not transgress.’”
